conclusions: The strongest new evidence concerns local implementation, procurement continuity, incentive payments, open-source diffusion, and network-launch attempts. It still does not establish WEF command authority or direct funding of the reviewed local programs.
findings: The identified HNTB Smart Lighting authorization chain totals $1,675,811.18.
AndHealth public payment records contain a reporting-year inconsistency requiring primary agreement and compliance records.
Green IT 2.0 specifies fourteen practices and links them to local execution services.
UrbanOS code replication is public; external production adoption remains unverified.
A Columbus Global Shapers launch received Cleveland support, but current official hub status was not verified.
Smart Columbus publishes a current role map for implementation functions.
No direct WEF–City payment or executed agreement was found in the bounded public review.
